title: UPSC CSAT Paper II — Hard Simulation 2

rubric.reasoning_layers: At least two linked deductions, constraints or conditional checks in every non-trivial item.
rubric.distractor_quality: All four options are plausible, distinct and comparable in visible length and specificity.
rubric.time_pressure: Complete paper: 80 questions in 120 minutes; revision drill: 40 questions in 75 minutes.

rubric.verification: Every keyed answer is recomputed or independently constraint-checked before PDF generation.

questions.text: Which interpretation most accurately states the main proposition of Passage 1? Use the forest-response dashboard as the complete information set for this question.
options: That technology adoption in small enterprises is mainly technical and therefore has no significant distributive consequences.
That technology adoption in small enterprises can be solved through one nationwide institutional reform under all conditions.
That technology adoption in small enterprises should be left to spontaneous private action without accountable public oversight.
That technology adoption in small enterprises requires aligned incentives, evidence and local feedback rather than one universal prescription.
questions.solution: The passage links the issue to incentives, evidence and feedback; the alternatives are absolute or narrowly framed.

questions.text: Which conclusion follows most securely from Passage 1? Use the school-recovery ledger as the complete information set for this question.
options: Administrative discretion is always harmful, even when evidence reveals local constraints.
Measurement adds little when an intervention has a persuasive and desirable objective.
An intervention may fail despite a desirable objective when its feedback loop remains weak.
A locally successful intervention will work identically elsewhere without any adaptation or review.
questions.solution: The passage distinguishes a desirable objective from the quality of its feedback loop; it rejects universal claims.

questions.text: Which presupposition is required by the argument in Passage 1? Use the municipal works map as the complete information set for this question.
options: Every measurable outcome is morally decisive regardless of the chosen public objective.
Institutional learning can improve policy without requiring perfect foresight at the outset.
Central rules are never useful, even when they protect minimum entitlements.
Local actors always possess complete information before implementation begins.
questions.solution: The argument depends on learning through feedback; it does not require perfect information or reject all central rules.

questions.text: Passage 1 adopts which overall rhetorical posture? Use the clinic-referral diary as the complete information set for this question.
options: Purely polemical and adversarial, treating competing approaches as illegitimate.

questions.solution: The wording weighs trade-offs and improvement mechanisms rather than celebrating, rejecting or attacking them.

questions.text: If r is the remainder when 7^25 + 8^23 is divided by 13, what is r? Use the ward-grievance register as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Compute powers modulo 13; cyclic reduction gives remainder 12.

questions.text: How many integers from 4 through 105, inclusive, are divisible by 7 or 10, but not by both? Use the coastal-service ledger as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Count multiples of 7 and 10, then remove twice the common multiples: the exclusive count is 23.

questions.text: Solution A contains 19% solute and solution B contains 22% solute. If A and B are mixed in the volume ratio 5:1, what is the resulting concentration? Use the hill-health register as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Use a weighted average: (5×19+22)/(5+1) = 19.50%.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a row. C is third from the left; A is left of D; B and F are non-adjacent; G is not at an end. Which person cannot occupy fifth position? Use the hostel attendance sheet as the complete information set for this question.
options: A
C
D
B
questions.solution: Enumerating all valid arrangements gives possible fifth-position occupants ['A', 'B', 'D', 'E', 'F', 'G']; C never appears there.

questions.text: Six candidates P, Q, R, S, T and U are ranked first to sixth. P is above R, R above U, S above R, Q below S, and T is not first. Which candidate cannot be third? Use the river-route log as the complete information set for this question.
options: U
R
Q
P
questions.solution: Testing all rankings gives possible third-place candidates ['P', 'Q', 'R', 'S', 'T']; U violates the partial-order constraints in every valid ranking.

questions.text: A field worker moves 7 km east and then 5 km north. What is the straight-line distance from the starting point, ignoring the path taken? Use the safety-inspection file as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Displacement = sqrt(7²+5²) = 8.60 km.

questions.text: M is the sister of N. N is the father of P. P is the daughter of Q. Relative to P, what is M? Use the forest-response dashboard as the complete information set for this question.
options: P's paternal cousin
P's paternal aunt
P's grandmother
P's maternal aunt
questions.solution: N is P's father; M is N's sister, so M is P's paternal aunt.

questions.text: Exactly one of A, B and C is guilty and exactly one statement is true. A says B is guilty; B says A and C are innocent; C says B is innocent. Who is guilty? Use the school-recovery ledger as the complete information set for this question.
options: No one
B only
A only
C only
questions.solution: Assume exactly one of A, B and C is guilty and exactly one statement is true. A says B is guilty; B says A and C are innocent; C says B is innocent. Testing A, B and C in turn leaves only B guilty: A and C are then false, while B is true.

questions.text: In a tribal sub-division, a file concerning hostel attendance is being reviewed by education supervisors; the available evidence includes monthly attendance sheets. A pilot produces mixed results across neighbourhoods. How should the administrator respond? Use the forest-response dashboard as the complete information set for this question.
options: Hide the mixed results until a later evaluation produces a simpler narrative.
Examine context-specific results, adapt the design and publish the decision rule.
Scale it everywhere immediately because any positive result proves universal effectiveness.
Cancel it everywhere immediately because variation means the intervention has failed.
questions.solution: Disaggregated evidence supports adaptation rather than premature scaling, cancellation or concealment.

questions.text: In a tribal sub-division, a file concerning hostel attendance is being reviewed by education supervisors; the available evidence includes monthly attendance sheets. A grievance channel receives fewer complaints after a redesign. What is the most careful interpretation? Use the school-recovery ledger as the complete information set for this question.
options: Conclude that the redesign failed because every effective channel should receive more complaints.
Check accessibility, repeat-use patterns and independent feedback before judging the change.
Conclude that service quality improved because fewer complaints always mean fewer problems.
Stop monitoring because the lower number already provides a sufficient success signal.
questions.solution: Complaint counts need accessibility and independent-feedback checks before they can indicate improvement.

Ask the contractor to proceed informally so that the paperwork does not delay work.

questions.solution: A documented risk and change-control assessment protects safety without making procedure an empty ritual.

questions.text: In a tribal sub-division, a file concerning hostel attendance is being reviewed by education supervisors; the available evidence includes monthly attendance sheets. questions.text: In a river island, a file concerning boat-based outreach is being reviewed by field coordinators; the available evidence includes route and turnout data.
